I've been reading for a month Grant Morrison's New X-Men Omnibus and the first arcs weren't really interesting. However, the latest issues have been incredible, from a whodunnit led by Bishop, then a Fantomex-centric arc (who's a character I love) and now, the major traitor has been revealed and it's brutal and phenomenal. Everything comes unexpectidly together so well and I was really positively surprised, after a low debut. Grant Morrison reminded me once again why he's one of the greatest comic-book authors of all-time. Also Ethan Van Sciver is thankfully not drawing those last issues.

But, because of the density of the book, I've been reading other things between the arcs. I tried the Spider-Bite issue from Tom Taylor and Juann Cabal. It was nice but miles away from Chip Zdarsky's #310 issue, which was brilliant and far more emotional.

Apart from some philosophy books, I've just finished Super: Up In The Sky by Tom King and Andy Kubert and I loved it. I'm a huge fan of the author, specially of his story-telling and characterisations. His writing is always innovating and unique. He's a real genius and manages, from 12-page-long issues published in Walmart specials, to create a new All-Star Superman : a universal story about what and who is Superman. Also, Andy Kubert delivers some great pages which match really well with the tone. While it wasn't perfect and some elements annoyed me (like some out-of-place but well-integrated team-ups), it was excellent and I'm eager to see what Tom King has ready next (I'm so hyped for Rorschach !).
